notes.title: v1.0.8: Spell Perks
notes.notes:
[h1]v1.0.8[/h1]
[h3][u]Features[/u][/h3]
[list]
[*] [b][u]Perks[/u][/b]: Upgrade your skills with minor and major perks. Major perks significantly improve the behavior of each spell.
[*] [b][u]New Trap[/u][/b]: Exploding mushrooms? They're purple, they glow, and they explode!
[/list]
[u]Major Perks[/u]
[list]
[*] [i]The following is a quick rundown of the major perks for each skill. There are also two minor perks which slightly improve the core skill.[/i]
[*] Fireball: Explodes on impact for additional area damage.
[*] Self Heal: Instantly heals for 100% health.
[*] Blast Wave: Casts a second ring of fire outside of the first after the first expires.
[*] Short Teleport: Teleporting deals damage around the hero at the start and end locations.
[*] Electric Fire: Splits into three separate blasts.
[*] Heat Shield: Deals damage to nearby enemies while active.
[*] Molten Core: Can hit a second enemy, both impacts with area damage.
[*] Fire Wall: Casts a second wall perpendicular to the first.
[/list]
[u]Improvements[/u]
[list]
[*] Simple tutorial tooltip when the first perk becomes available.
[*] Can drag the perk to the skill bar to activate that spell.
[*] Reworked projectile casting to support perks.
[*] When opening windows, the most recently opened window will show up on top.
[*] Dragging a spell off the skill bar will remove it from the skill bar.
[*] Dragging spells between slots will swap their positions.
[*] Triggering a boss encounter and being locked out of the encounter area will now allow the encounter to reset.
[*] Minor visual fix to incorrect minimap visual in crypts.
[/list]
[h2]Developer's Note[/h2]

Spell perks are a major new feature. They vastly expand the various configurations available to load out your hero. You can set up your hero with different focuses, from an AOE damage focus, to a mobility focus, to a defensive focus, to a single target focus. Let me know what you think!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39302666/76f9938a9f619e0d5ba381a0b1066931d9232ed4.jpg[/img]

Hope you enjoy the changes.

- Sarynth

notes.title: Dungeons Underway
notes.notes:
As a first step towards some randomized play areas, the crypt area in the cemetery will see our first procedural dungeon show up in the next release.

Lots of work has gone into integrating a wonderful third party asset, Dungeon Architect. It is now deeply tied into the core code base. The hope is that it will also come into play with some of the open world areas as well, but that's still in the concept phase.

A secondary effort that was required to support these dungeons is a completely reworked checkpoint system. From the user point of view, things will be fairly similar. Checkpoints will still be unlocked, and teleported between.

What's new is session persistence. If you have cleared an area, teleport away, then teleport back, those creatures will still be cleared. This was important so that when you go into the crypt/dungeon, then return to the main map -- all of the creatures won't suddenly respawn and ambush you at the entrance.

If you do want to reset all of the creatures, you can return to the main menu, and continue your game. The session will refresh and you'll have a full set of enemies to vanquish.

Oh, and one more little thing. Sneak peek below. Coming soon...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39302666/c935ce24eeae946461cc74a26b359848fce6ef47.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Dev Log: Frame Rate Frustration
notes.notes:
TL; DR. Success! Much improved frame rates in the Manamancer Boss fight with v1.0.3 release.

[h1]FPS Woes[/h1]

As I was recently expanding the playable area in the Mountain Pass scene, as usual I was doing some play testing. When testing the boss fight again, the lag was sticking out as a major issue.

I had been putting this off for a while, but it finally bubbled to the top of an enjoyable play experience for me. So, I dove into it. I started reviewing the profiler, turning various features in the fight area things on and off.

The profiler shot below shows there was clearly an issue.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39302666/1ba90c38bf412aee0ca6f38d0c5982f028b4cc2c.jpg[/img]

The large green bumps at the top of the profiler showed that the CPU was waiting for the GPU to finish it's thing. I have a pretty decent GPU, so I would not have thought that would be a problem. Starting to investigate, someone on Discord (Thanks @Invertex) suggested checking out overdraw. Good idea!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39302666/214c1bc65701bc30059416d8df30a6e4e3a5f932.jpg[/img]

The particles for the corrupted spray that the boss uses creates an insane amount of draw calls. I mean, it sure is pretty though, isn't it?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39302666/db7ed00d5d0ba7cf7d0bd11147b3f5a175ca3fcd.jpg[/img]

I thought I had found the problem. I turned off ALL particles. Went in to play. 5fps. [b]What?![/b]

At this point I was desperate. I started doing what I've done since high school.

Binary search tree.

I turned off half the things in the fight, Did that solve it? If so, turn those back on, split them in half, and turn off half. If not, turn off the other half to verify that solves it, then split the other half in half and repeat.

Took a few minutes. Then, finally, the light at the end of the tunnel.

[h3]A Point Light[/h3]

One small measly point light that was nested deep within the hierarchy of the torches in the arena. The point light gave a small little glow to the inside of the torches. It had a radius of 8, so they overlapped a little. Multiple that by about 8 torches, and it absolutely wrecked havoc on the GPU.

I deleted the point light from the prefab, which removed it from all of the torches. Hit play, and suddenly everything was screaming along at full speed. Wow.

I turned some of the particle emission rates back up, and even with all of the beautiful particles, the FPS stayed above 100.

Problem solved, but boy I need to be more careful with point lights.

[i]-Sarynth[/i]

notes.title: Mana Gloom Releases December 29th!
notes.notes:
Get ready to engage in epic battles with corrupted spell casters. The mana stream has been infused with what the citizens have begun to call, Mana Gloom.

Wishlist this title and get ready for December 29th as it releases on Steam for Windows.

[h2]About the Developer[/h2]

Hello Adventurers!

I'm Sarynth. I've been working on games, from text based games to custom maps for nearly twenty years. I've always focused on building things that I enjoyed playing. Mana Gloom is no different.

My favorite aspect of many games is the boss fights, and that is where a lot of time and attention is focused. I hope you enjoy the various dynamics that enter into the boss fights, and I look forward to releasing more as time permits.

Please do share your favorite moments and biggest frustrations. I am listening! My initial focus is on quality gameplay and fight mechanics. There is no loot or inventory. There are no spell trees, experience systems or leveling. Just jump into the fight and start blasting enemies.

Enjoy!
[i]-Sarynth[/i]

notes.title: Dev Log: Emission and Bloom
notes.notes:
Sometimes I wonder myself, what takes so long to develop a game? Within a few hours of starting your project, you can have a character in a world, running around an island, swinging a sword. It shouldn't take that much longer to round it out and ship it. Right?

Let me tell you something... it's about the details. It's about the immersion. It's about the complete package. Some of the many things that go into that are emission and bloom. While it is easy to go overboard with these, without them things are pretty bland.

Take a look at these examples. In this first image, there is no bloom, and no emission.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39302666/dfe040e6c969a86eeac4bf47a49cc11ed3a6c5fb.png[/img]

Neat model, right? I thought so. Let's add in some bloom, and overall post-processing effects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39302666/0630797705a874fb1a060b79f2c321f2fb475352.png[/img]

Okay, we gained a little bit of ambiance. Something is still missing. I tried adjusting a few settings in the shaders, but it still didn't pop the way I wanted. Finally I decided to pull open the base texture, and make my own emissive map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39302666/27f9087b634312a8a2f0abb43c23502b9b74727e.png[/img]

Now we're talking. Look at that crystal glow! But, in the above screenshot, bloom had been turned off again, since my test scene has the camera effects typically turned off. So while it certainly had a vibrant blue hue, it still had just a little bit missing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39302666/278383e64b314b07f7eed0d7a6beed436245a0a6.png[/img]

And, there it is. Bloom and emission. Isn't it beautiful?

As some folks on reddit have said about other examples like this, "That is so pretty, now you need to make an entire game around it!"

Sometimes elements like this are motivational, as they look awesome. It all just takes time.

I hope that the little things like this help take a good game and make it great. While my main focus is making the primary game play fun, it also should look nice, and provide a complete experience. Things like this really bring out the ambiance, but also make the game take time.

[i]-Sarynth[/i]
